    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The full-width solid-color line is the separator; copy the populated
    # two-dimensional panel across the blank panel on the other side.
    sep = next((r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1), None)
    if sep is None or sep == 0 or sep == h - 1:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    bg = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row), key=lambda v: sum(x == v for row in grid for x in row))
    panels = [grid[:sep], grid[sep+1:]]

        return [row[:] for row in grid]

        if not any(v != bg for row in panel for v in row):
            start = 0 if idx == 0 else sep + 1
            for dr, row in enumerate(populated[:len(panel)]):
                out[start + dr] = row[:]
    return out

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The divider color is the uniform separator, while the most frequent
    # non-divider color is the background. Copy the marked tile to its mate.
    divrow = next((r for r,row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1), None)
    if divrow is None:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    sep = grid[divrow][0]
    vals = [x for row in grid for x in row if x != sep]
    if not vals:
        return [row[:] for row in grid]
    bg = max(set(vals), key=vals.count)
    result = [row[:] for row in grid]
    top, bottom = grid[:divrow], grid[divrow+1:]
    source = top if any(x != bg for row in top for x in row) else bottom
    target_start = divrow+1 if source is top else 0
    target_len = len(bottom) if source is top else len(top)
    if any(x != bg for row in source for x in row):
        for k in range(target_len):
            result[target_start+k] = source[k % len(source)][:]
    return result
PY
